organism_context: Corynebacterium glutamicum / Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Corynebacterineae lipomannan-lipoarabinomannan pathway)
rationale: EC 2.4.1.199 is beta-D-mannosylphosphodecaprenol:(1->6)-alpha-D-mannosyloligosaccharide 6-alpha-mannosyltransferase, i.e. a PPM-consuming GT-C membrane enzyme (MptA/MptB class) that elongates the alpha1,6-mannan backbone; it carries one catalytic activity, with the extra transmembrane region being structural, not a second active site.
direction_note: Mannosylphosphodecaprenol is the glycosyl DONOR and decaprenyl phosphate the leaving product, so the reaction runs left-to-right as written; ModelSEED's '<' has it synthesising PPM, which is a different enzyme (Ppm1) entirely. The mannooligosaccharide acceptor was dropped from both sides (MSDB flags MI C:-6/H:-11/O:-5).

enzyme_name: peptidoglycan glycosyltransferase (transglycosylase) domain of a class A penicillin-binding protein, PBP1b/PBP1a
organism_context: Escherichia coli class A PBPs are genuine single-chain GTase+TPase fusions; monofunctional glycosyltransferases also exist (MtgA, and the SEDS polymerases RodA/FtsW)
rationale: The crystal structure of E. coli PBP1b is titled and characterised as a membrane-bound bifunctional transglycosylase, with the glycosyltransferase and transpeptidase active sites on one polypeptide; the glycan-polymerising half catalyses this reaction.
direction_note: The GT domain polymerises lipid II and releases undecaprenyl-pyrophosphate, so lipid II (left) is the substrate; KEGG R06178 carries the growing glycan on both sides and ModelSEED dropped it, leaving MI C:-39/H:-63/N:-8/O:-19, and the cited EC 2.4.1.129 has itself been transferred to EC 2.4.99.28.

rationale: The entry is a fragment ('H2O + ATP <= Phosphate') with no name, no xref and only a partial EC; ADP is missing (MSDB MI C:-10/H:-14/N:-5/O:-10/P:-2), so no particular protein can be assigned.
direction_note: Whatever the EC 3.6.1.- hydrolase is, it consumes ATP + H2O (the left side here); ModelSEED's '<' would have inorganic phosphate condense into ATP, which no hydrolase does.

organism_context: human lysosomal membrane (deficiency causes mucopolysaccharidosis IIIC / Sanfilippo C)
rationale: HGSNAT is a polytopic lysosomal membrane protein with a single transmembrane acetyltransferase activity operating by a ping-pong acetyl-enzyme mechanism; the co-listed EC 2.3.1.79 (maltose O-acetyltransferase) is a spurious second assignment on this ModelSEED entry, not a second domain of the same protein.
direction_note: Acetyl-CoA is the acetyl donor and CoA the product, so the transfer runs left-to-right; the glucosamine acceptor was stripped (MI C:-2/H:-2/O:-1), leaving a bare acetyl-CoA/CoA pair whose direction ModelSEED then got backwards.

organism_context: E. coli WaaA transfers two Kdo residues with different regiochemistry on one chain; Aquifex aeolicus and Bordetella pertussis WaaA are monofunctional, and Chlamydiaceae enzymes are tri-/tetrafunctional
rationale: The record has no name, EC or xref, but the mass deficit is exactly one Kdo residue (C8H12O7) released from CMP-Kdo, which identifies it as a Kdo transfer rather than CMP-Kdo synthetase (no phosphate deficit); enzyme identity is therefore inferred from chemistry, while the mono-/bi-/trifunctional split among WaaA orthologues is well documented.
direction_note: Every WaaA variant, mono- or bifunctional, consumes CMP-Kdo and releases CMP, so the lineage differences in functionality do not bear on direction; the lipid IVA acceptor is absent from the equation.

organism_context: presumed plant (Lathyrus/Vicia beta-aminopropionitrile chemistry)
rationale: The mass deficit is exactly CO2 (MSDB MI C:-1/H:1/O:-2, CI:1), so the step is decarboxylation of L-3-cyanoalanine to 3-aminopropionitrile, but searches of PubMed and Europe PMC returned no characterised cyanoalanine decarboxylase, so no protein can be named or classified.
direction_note: Decarboxylations are effectively irreversible in the CO2-releasing sense, which here is left-to-right (cyanoalanine -> aminopropionitrile); the missing CO2 is what lets ModelSEED read the equation backwards.

enzyme_name: nogalonic acid methyl ester synthase SnoaC (SAM-dependent O-methyltransferase)
organism_context: Streptomyces nogalater nogalamycin biosynthetic cluster; KEGG orthologue K15942 also covers the related aklanonic acid methyltransferases (DnrC/StfMI)
rationale: KEGG R06675 names the catalyst as 'methyltransferase, snoaC', a stand-alone small SAM-dependent O-methyltransferase in the 20-kb nogalamycin cluster; no second catalytic domain is reported for it.
direction_note: SAM-dependent methyl transfer (SAM -> SAH) is thermodynamically one-way in the methylating sense, which is left-to-right as written.

rationale: KEGG R06850 carries the explicit COMMENT 'unclear reaction', no EC and no KO, and the ModelSEED copy gains a chlorine from nowhere (MI Cl:-1/H:1); there is no enzyme to classify.
direction_note: KEGG itself disowns the entry as an unclear reaction with no catalyst, so neither the ModelSEED nor the LLM direction is meaningful.

enzyme_name: unidentified 3-oxosteroid 3beta-reductase ('campestanol synthase') acting downstream of the DET2 steroid 5alpha-reductase
organism_context: Arabidopsis thaliana / Pisum sativum brassinosteroid biosynthesis
rationale: The brassinosteroid pathway is well mapped (DET2 makes 5alpha-campestan-3-one, which is then reduced to campestanol), but the 3-ketoreductase gene has not been cloned, and KEGG R07466 carries no EC or KO at all.
direction_note: KEGG flags R07466 as an 'incomplete reaction' and the hydride donor (NADPH) is absent, leaving a bare 2 H+ (MSDB CI:-2); pathway flux nevertheless runs campestan-3-one -> campestanol, i.e. left-to-right.

enzyme_name: unidentified 3-oxosteroid 3alpha-reductase of the teasterone/typhasterol epimerisation step
organism_context: Arabidopsis thaliana and other plants, brassinosteroid biosynthesis
rationale: The 3-dehydroteasterone -> typhasterol reduction is an established pathway step but no gene product has been assigned to it; KEGG R07469 lists no EC and no orthology, so the catalysing protein cannot be classified.
direction_note: Biosynthetic flux runs teasterone -> 3-dehydroteasterone -> typhasterol, i.e. the reductive left-to-right sense here; the NAD(P)H donor has been replaced by a bare 2 H+ (MSDB CI:-2), which is what leaves the direction underdetermined.

enzyme_name: unidentified 3-oxosteroid 3beta-reductase of the early C-22 oxidation branch
organism_context: Arabidopsis thaliana brassinosteroid biosynthesis (early C-22 oxidation route)
rationale: 22alpha-hydroxy-5alpha-campestan-3-one -> 6-deoxocathasterone is a 3-keto reduction in the early C-22 oxidation branch; KEGG R07472 lists only a literature citation, no EC and no orthology, so the enzyme is unidentified.
direction_note: The pathway consumes the 3-ketone and makes the 3beta-ol (left-to-right); the NADPH donor is missing and only 2 H+ remain (MSDB CI:-2).

organism_context: Arabidopsis thaliana and other plants, brassinosteroid biosynthesis (late C-6 oxidation route)
rationale: 3-dehydro-6-deoxoteasterone -> 6-deoxotyphasterol parallels the teasterone/typhasterol step and has no assigned gene product; KEGG R07473 carries no EC and no orthology.
direction_note: Flux runs 6-deoxoteasterone -> 3-dehydro-6-deoxoteasterone -> 6-deoxotyphasterol, so the reductive left-to-right sense is the physiological one; the hydride donor is absent (MSDB CI:-2).

organism_context: Arabidopsis thaliana and other plants/algae (the SMT1 paralogue acting on cycloartenol); fungal ERG6 is the homologue
rationale: SAM:cycloartenol C-24-methyltransferase carries a single methyl-transfer activity via a high-energy carbocation intermediate; some SMTs perform a second (C-28) methylation, but that is the same catalytic activity on a different substrate, not a second active site.
direction_note: SAM-dependent C-methylation through a carbocation intermediate is irreversible in the methylating direction, which is left-to-right here (SAM + cycloartenol -> SAH + 24-methylenecycloartanol); the equation itself is balanced (MSDB status OK).

enzyme_name: Delta7-sterol reductase / 7-dehydrocholesterol reductase (DWF5 in plants, DHCR7 in animals)
organism_context: Arabidopsis thaliana DWF5 (dwarf mutant blocked in brassinosteroid/sterol biosynthesis); human DHCR7 is the orthologue (Smith-Lemli-Opitz)
rationale: KEGG R07492 maps to EC 1.3.1.21 / K00213, a single-activity NADPH-dependent polytopic membrane sterol reductase; no second catalytic activity is reported.
direction_note: The enzyme reduces the Delta7 bond of 5-dehydroepisterol to give 24-methylenecholesterol, i.e. left-to-right; NADPH has been replaced by a bare 2 H+ (MSDB CI:-2), which removes the driver that makes the reduction one-way.

enzyme_name: 3-keto-steroid reductase (3-KSR): HSD17B7 in mammals, Erg27p in yeast
organism_context: The mammalian protein HSD17B7 is bifunctional (IUBMB notes this explicitly under EC 1.1.1.270); the Saccharomyces cerevisiae orthologue Erg27p carries only the 3-ketoreductase activity
rationale: Human HSD17B7, identified as the missing 3-ketosteroid reductase of cholesterol biosynthesis, also runs estrone -> 17beta-estradiol on the same polypeptide, and inhibitor studies show its multiple catalytic activities respond differently; this is one reaction of the C4-demethylation sequence that it performs.
direction_note: Both HSD17B7 activities are NADPH-dependent ketone reductions, so bifunctionality does not pull the direction either way; IUBMB states that in sterol biosynthesis the enzyme runs opposite to the written dehydrogenation, i.e. 3-keto-4-methylzymosterol -> 4-methylzymosterol (left-to-right), and the ModelSEED equation puts NADP+/NADPH on the wrong sides (MSDB CI:-4).

enzyme_name: Delta24-sterol reductase (DHCR24/seladin-1 in mammals, Erg4p in yeast)
organism_context: mammals (DHCR24, desmosterolosis) and fungi (ERG4)
rationale: EC 1.3.1.72 is a single-activity FAD/NADPH-dependent sterol Delta24 reductase acting on a range of 24(25)-ene sterols including zymosterol; DHCR24's reported neuroprotective 'seladin-1' role is a moonlighting function, not a second catalytic activity, so it stays monofunctional. Called from the IUBMB entry and standard sterol biochemistry rather than a new search.
direction_note: Physiological flux is the reduction zymosterol -> zymostenol, which is left-to-right as written; ModelSEED has NADP+ paired with the diene and NADPH with the saturated product, inverting the redox bookkeeping (MSDB CI:-4) and so inverting the apparent direction.

organism_context: Saccharomyces cerevisiae and other fungi (ergosterol biosynthesis); KEGG orthologue K09831
rationale: KEGG R07506 assigns EC 1.14.19.41 / K09831, a single-active-site microsomal P450; its electron donor NADPH-cytochrome P450 reductase is a separate polypeptide, not a fused domain, and the reported xenobiotic turnover is substrate promiscuity rather than a second activity.
direction_note: KEGG's real equation is 5-dehydroepisterol + NADPH + H+ + O2 -> ergosta-5,7,22,24(28)-tetraenol + NADP+ + 2 H2O, so the triene (left) is the substrate; once O2 and the two waters are deleted the entry degenerates into a reversible-looking NADP+ dehydrogenation with the nicotinamide cofactors flipped, and ModelSEED's '<' is an artefact of that.

enzyme_name: phytoene desaturase (PDS), with zeta-carotene isomerase (Z-ISO) supplying the cis-configuration change
organism_context: plants and cyanobacteria (plastoquinone-dependent poly-cis desaturation pathway)
rationale: Plant PDS is a single-activity plastoquinone-linked flavoprotein that performs two identical desaturations (15-cis-phytoene -> 9,15,9'-tri-cis-zeta-carotene); reaching the 9,9'-di-cis isomer written here additionally requires the separate Z-ISO gene product, so the entry collapses two enzymes but each one is monofunctional.
direction_note: Desaturation runs phytoene -> zeta-carotene (left-to-right); the free H2 in the ModelSEED equation stands in for the plastoquinone acceptor whose reoxidation makes the step one-way.

organism_context: plants and cyanobacteria; the EC 1.14.99.30 attached by ModelSEED is bacterial CrtI, which does not make these poly-cis intermediates
rationale: ZDS is one plastoquinone-dependent desaturase that performs the two successive desaturations 9,9'-di-cis-zeta-carotene -> 7,9,9'-tri-cis-neurosporene -> 7,9,7',9'-tetra-cis-lycopene; iterating the same chemistry is a single catalytic activity, not bifunctionality.
direction_note: Flux is zeta-carotene -> prolycopene (left-to-right); free H2 replaces the plastoquinone/FAD acceptor, removing the thermodynamic driver that forbids the reverse.

enzyme_name: carotene 3,4-desaturase of the CrtI/CrtD flavoprotein family (e.g. the five-step desaturase AL-1/CarB, or CrtD)
organism_context: fungi (Neurospora AL-1, Fusarium CarB) and purple/photosynthetic bacteria (CrtD)
rationale: The chemistry (lycopene -> 3,4-didehydrolycopene) is a single FAD-dependent desaturation carried out by CrtI-family enzymes; these enzymes repeat the same desaturation on successive bonds, which is one catalytic activity, but the record has no EC detail or xref so the specific protein is inferred.
direction_note: Carotenogenesis runs lycopene -> 3,4-didehydrolycopene (left-to-right); the equation releases free H2 instead of reducing the real FAD/quinone acceptor.

organism_context: purple photosynthetic bacteria (Rhodospirillum rubrum, Rubrivivax) spirilloxanthin pathway; Synechocystis Slr1293 is the cyanobacterial C-3',4' desaturase
rationale: Rhodopin -> 3,4-didehydrorhodopin is the canonical CrtD step of the spirilloxanthin pathway, a single-activity flavin desaturase acting on 1-hydroxy carotenoids.
direction_note: Biosynthetic flux runs rhodopin -> 3,4-didehydrorhodopin (left-to-right); free H2 stands in for the real electron acceptor, and the equation is also charge-unbalanced (MSDB CI:-2).

organism_context: purple photosynthetic bacteria, late spirilloxanthin pathway
rationale: Rhodovibrin -> hydroxyspirilloxanthin is another 3,4-desaturation on a 1-hydroxy/1-methoxy carotenoid, the same CrtD activity as the earlier rhodopin step; the record carries no xref, so the assignment is from the chemistry and pathway position.
direction_note: Flux runs rhodovibrin -> the 3,4-didehydro product (left-to-right); free H2 replaces the real acceptor.

organism_context: Rhodobacter spheroidene pathway (chloroxanthin -> demethylspheroidene)
rationale: Chloroxanthin (1-HO-1,2-dihydroneurosporene) -> demethylspheroidene is the defining CrtD 3,4-desaturation of the spheroidene branch, a single flavin-dependent desaturase activity.
direction_note: Flux runs chloroxanthin -> demethylspheroidene (left-to-right); the free H2 product is a stand-in for the real electron acceptor.

organism_context: Arabidopsis thaliana (abscisic acid catabolism); homologous PA reductases in strawberry
rationale: CRL1 was identified as the PA reductase that catalyses phaseic acid -> dihydrophaseic acid, a single NADPH-dependent reduction in a CCR-like oxidoreductase with Tyr162 as the catalytic residue; no second activity is reported.
direction_note: ABA catabolism runs PA -> DPA, the reductive left-to-right sense here; NADPH is absent from the equation and only a bare 2 H+ remains (MSDB CI:-2).

enzyme_name: carotenoid glucosyltransferase (CrtX-type) plus the carotenoid-glucoside acyltransferase CruC
organism_context: Thermus thermophilus (thermozeaxanthin/thermocryptoxanthin glucoside-ester carotenoids)
rationale: The mass deficit (C17H30O6) is a glucosyl residue plus a C11 acyl group, so the entry collapses two separate transfer steps - glucosylation of beta-cryptoxanthin and acylation of that glucose (the latter lost in a Thermus cruC deletion mutant) - and no single protein catalyses it, so neither can be classified.
direction_note: Biosynthesis runs beta-cryptoxanthin -> glucoside -> acylated thermocryptoxanthin, i.e. left-to-right; both missing donors (UDP-glucose and the acyl donor) are what make each real step irreversible.
